6.3 · The state

The whole agent is one folder.

Identity, memory, skills, schedules, every conversation it's ever had — all of it lives in ~/.hermes. Own the folder, own the agent.

▎ think of it like

A passport folder.

Everything that makes it your agent, in one place. Carry the folder and the agent moves with you.

~/.hermes/ · the whole brain
~/.hermes/
├── config.yaml     ← models, memory, gateway
├── .env            ← every API key (chmod 600)
├── SOUL.md         ← who it is
├── memories/       ← MEMORY.md · USER.md
├── skills/         ← everything it's learned to do
├── cron/           ← the schedules
├── sessions/       ← every conversation (SQLite)
├── logs/           ← incl. the Curator's receipts
└── backups/        ← hermes backup lands here
🎒
Why this makes migration trivial

hermes backup archives the folder, timestamped. hermes import restores it anywhere. The agent IS the folder — which is exactly why the next lesson works.

So what →

Run hermes backup right now — before this chapter touches anything. That archive is your agent's passport. Treat it like one.

6.4 · The migration

Move the brain. Keep the window.

Your agent moves to a small server that never sleeps. Your laptop stops being the brain and becomes just a window on it.

▎ think of it like

Moving day for a brain.

The mind gets crated, hoisted, and installed in a building with generators. You keep your keys.

1
Harden

Ubuntu 24.04, non-root user, SSH keys only, firewall allows port 22. Nothing else.

10 min
2
Install

The one-line installer, then hermes doctor to prove it's healthy.

5 min
3
Move

backup → scp → import. The passport flies. Lock .env to 600.

10 min
4
Own

Stop the desktop agent. The VPS owns the brain now; the laptop copy is a backup.

the rule
5
Persist

hermes gateway install + linger — it survives reboots and logouts.

5 min
6
Reach

Tailscale on server, laptop, phone. Next lesson — the best part.

10 min
7
Prove

Reboot the box. Everything comes back. Nightly backups rsync off-box.

the test
the whole migration · four commandsdesktop → vps
# on the desktop — crate the brain
$ hermes backup
$ scp ~/.hermes/backups/hermes-backup-<stamp>.tar.gz you@vps:~

# on the VPS — install it, make it permanent
$ hermes import ~/hermes-backup-<stamp>.tar.gz && chmod 600 ~/.hermes/.env
$ hermes gateway install && sudo loginctl enable-linger $USER
🧩
The one known gap — and the one-line fix

The gateway has an official service installer; the dashboard doesn't (open issue on GitHub). After a reboot the agent returns but the dashboard won't. Fix: one tiny extra systemd user unit running hermes dashboard --no-open — and the same trick runs the OS console on the box.

So what →

Block out a Sunday coffee: the whole move is about 45 minutes, once. From then on your agent works nights, survives reboots, and doesn't care where your laptop is.

6.5 · The private door

Your own private internet.

Tailscale puts your laptop, your phone and the server on one invisible network — encrypted device-to-device, with nothing exposed to the public web.

▎ think of it like

A members-only tunnel ring.

Your three devices hold the only keys. The open internet rages outside the ring and never gets a door handle.

🩹
The 60-second wayssh tunnel · the demo
  • ssh -L 9119:127.0.0.1:9119 you@vps — dashboard on localhost, instantly
  • Dies the moment your laptop sleeps
  • No phone. No permanence. A demo, not a door.
🔐
The right waytailscale · the door
  • Install on server + laptop + phone, log in once each
  • Every device gets a stable private 100.x address — and a name
  • Survives sleep, roams networks, works from the beach
what it is

WireGuard, minus the pain

A mesh VPN: every device connects directly to every other, encrypted end-to-end. The coordination server only introduces them — your traffic never touches it.

🧭
how you use it

Names, not numbers

MagicDNS means the server is just http://vps:9119 from any of your devices. Type it on your phone. That's the whole workflow.

🚪
why it's safe

Zero open ports

It punches through NAT outbound — so the firewall stays sealed shut. To the public internet your server is a locked box with no doors, SSH aside.

1
One account

Sign up at tailscale.com with Google or GitHub. The free plan covers 100 devices — you need 3.

2 min
2
VPS joins

Run the installer on the server, then sudo tailscale up — it prints a login link, open it, approve.

2 min
3
Laptop joins

Install the desktop app (or brew install tailscale), sign in to the same account. It appears in the device list.

2 min
4
Phone joins

App Store / Play Store → Tailscale → same sign-in. Flip the toggle on. That's the pocket window.

2 min
5
Name it

In the admin console check MagicDNS is on (it is by default) — your server is now just vps, no IP to memorize.

1 min
6
Prove it

On the phone, on mobile data, open http://vps:9119. Dashboard loads → the ring is closed.

the moment
steps 2, 5 & 6 · the exact commandsvps
# step 2 — on the VPS
$ curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sh
$ sudo tailscale up          # prints the login link → approve in browser

# step 5 — sanity checks
$ tailscale status            # all three devices listed?
$ tailscale ip -4             # the server's private 100.x address

# step 6 — from laptop or phone, anywhere on earth
$ open http://vps:9119        # dashboard · MagicDNS name

# optional flourish — a proper https:// URL, still private
$ tailscale serve --bg 9119   # → https://vps.your-tailnet.ts.net
🔒 sealed end-to-end

Nobody reads the wire

WireGuard encryption, device to device. Tailscale's servers only introduce your machines — your traffic never touches them.

🫥 invisible outside

No door to attack

Zero open ports, so port scanners sweep past and find nothing. You can't brute-force a login page that doesn't exist.

🪪 devices, not passwords

Only your hardware gets in

Access is tied to devices signed into your account. Laptop stolen? Revoke it from the console in one click — it's off the net instantly.

🌍 works anywhere

No router surgery

Hotel Wi-Fi, mobile data, double-NAT — it punches through. No port forwarding, no static IP, no ISP phone calls.

🧾 one-glance audit

You can see the whole net

The admin console lists every device on your tailnet. If something's there that isn't yours, you kick it — that's the entire audit.

💸 free for this

$0 for your whole setup

The personal plan covers 3 users and 100 devices. A laptop, a phone and a server don't even scratch it.

Add it up: your agent's dashboard — the thing that can read every key you own — is reachable by exactly three devices on Earth, and by nothing else.

So what →

Install Tailscale on the server and your phone tonight. The first time you open your agent's dashboard from a café on mobile data, always-on stops being a concept.

6.6 · Lockdown

Locked by default.

An always-on agent is an always-on attack surface. Four things you never do, six boxes you always tick.

☠️
Neverthe corruption & the leak
  • Two-way sync of ~/.hermes between machines — live SQLite + two writers = corrupted memory. One machine owns the brain.
  • sshfs-mounting server state into a desktop agent
  • --insecure or binding the dashboard to 0.0.0.0 — it can read .env, i.e. every key you own
  • GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS — ever
✅
Alwaysthe six boxes
  • SSH keys only · firewall default-deny (22 open, nothing else)
  • Gateway and dashboard reachable via Tailscale only — never public
  • chmod 600 ~/.hermes/.env
  • Per-platform user allowlists on the gateway
  • approval_mode: ask or Docker terminal for a box that runs unsupervised
  • Backups contain secrets — encrypt them before they leave the box
So what →

Do the six boxes before the first night it runs alone. Security added later is security that wasn't there when it mattered.
